definitions.explanation: A green bell pepper. In Japanese, ピーマン typically refers to the smaller, thinner-walled green peppers common in Asian cooking rather than the larger Western bell peppers.

examples.japanese: ピーマンの{肉|にく}{詰|づ}めを{作|つく}った。
{子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}はピーマンが{苦手|にがて}だった。
examples.english: I didn't like green peppers when I was a kid.

examples.japanese: ピーマンとパプリカを{細切|ほそぎ}りにして{炒|いた}め{物|もの}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I julienned green peppers and paprika and added them to the stir-fry.

notes:
USAGE:
ピーマン is one of the most commonly disliked vegetables among Japanese children, frequently appearing in surveys of children's least favorite foods. Common dishes include ピーマンの{肉|にく}{詰|づ}め (meat-stuffed peppers) and {青椒|チンジャオ}ロースー (pepper steak stir-fry).

NOTE ON SCOPE:
Larger, colorful bell peppers (red, yellow, orange) are usually called パプリカ in Japanese, while ピーマン refers to the smaller green variety.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ピーマンの{肉|にく}{詰|づ}め (meat-stuffed green peppers)
- ピーマンを{炒|いた}める (stir-fry green peppers)
- ピーマンの{種|たね}を{取|と}る (remove green pepper seeds)

ETYMOLOGY:
From French "piment" (pepper).
